authorization_reference: User: Launch training. Consecutive in-scope scratch experiments under program.md.
budget_rationale: One additional execution comparison after width192 microbatch16 measured 3.1484 s/update (34.982 optimizer hours). Width192 batch32 inference measured 0.2052/0.8200 s at one/four calls versus width160 0.3779/1.5099, showing a changed execution path; S2 also showed large full-update microbatch sensitivity. Up to 900 cumulative GPU-job seconds covers contracts and one 115-update batch32 probe with no further fallback or sweep. Prior qualification cost is retained.
selection_rule: Choose microbatch32 for production only if its measured full-update mean and terminal mean are each at least 5% faster than qualified microbatch16, peak allocation is below 18GB, and numerical/contracts pass. Otherwise retain16. Effective batch stays128. This is a new declared bounded execution comparison, not a renewal of the first qualification allowance.
production_initialization: New random initialization at update zero after qualification; no qualification weights, optimizer, EMA, RNG or data state are reused.
decision_question: Whether microbatch32 materially improves the width192 full training-update time before allocating a 40k production run; no candidate FID.
